investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes are excluded by node affinity or selector rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every remote agent pod creation attempt is immediately marked Unschedulable, the VM is never started, and the eval runner never receives the agent identity or VM state needed to satisfy the expected-output contract. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected failure.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration that over-constrains scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes: if the affinity rules are too narrow, even a partially loaded cluster will appear exhausted. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — a quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or cluster level that caps total allocations below current demand. Not directly evidenced but consistent with the scheduler message.

QUATERNARY — a node or daemonset managing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (e.g., a peer-pods device plugin) is unhealthy or not advertising capacity on the two matching nodes. Consistent with the message but not directly evidenced in this packet.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the two affinity-matching nodes show available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduler or admission issue should be investigated.

If a subsequent eval run with no other changes passes and produces vmIdPresent===true and a valid remoteState, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly leaked pod released its VM slot) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the pod's node affinity or selector is found to match more than 2 of the 6 nodes in the cluster, the '4 node(s) didn't match' clause would indicate a node labeling regression rather than a capacity problem on the correct nodes.

If the kata.peerpods.io/vm device plugin or peer-pods daemonset is found to be healthy and advertising full capacity on both matching nodes, the root cause would shift to a quota or namespace-level resource limit rather than node-level exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed in the same run window, the failure would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared scheduling constraint.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on all cluster nodes, alerting before full exhaustion rather than only after a scheduling failure.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the remote agent pod's affinity/selector matches at least a configurable minimum number of nodes (e.g., >= 3), catching over-constrained affinity rules before they cause scheduling failures.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that checks for remote agent pods in terminal states (Completed, Error, OOMKilled) that are still holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations and have exceeded a maximum age threshold.

Add a kata.peerpods.io/vm device plugin health eval that checks the peer-pods daemonset pod status on all kata-capable nodes and alerts if any instance is not Running, catching capacity advertisement failures before they exhaust the scheduler pool.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient VM quota and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to report all four required evidence fields as missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have no remaining capacity, and the remaining four nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or label selector constraints. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers a peer-pod VM provisioning request that the scheduler cannot fulfill. The pod remains Unschedulable for the full 145-second observation window, so the probe exits without writing any evidence, and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264 (requiredEvidence: orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agent VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract at line 264 requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none of which can be populated without a running agent VM.

source.check-config.remote-agent-state: check is marked required:true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latencyMs=150171 is well within the outage threshold, so the failure is a hard scheduling block, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs from prior runs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires labels or taints (e.g., a kata-peerpods node pool label) that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity, making the effective schedulable pool size 0.

Tertiary — VM pool scaling lag or autoscaler not configured: the cluster may lack a node autoscaler for the kata-peerpods node pool, so capacity is not automatically added when the quota is exhausted.

Lower confidence — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from previous eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime passed, the failure would be isolated to the state-polling logic rather than VM scheduling capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes are excluded by node affinity or selector rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every remote agent pod creation attempt is immediately marked Unschedulable, the VM is never started, and the eval runner never receives the agent identity or VM state needed to satisfy the expected-output contract. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected failure.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 0/6 nodes, latencyMs=150219

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract asserts vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration that over-constrains scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes: if the affinity rules are too narrow, even a partially loaded cluster will appear exhausted. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — a quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or cluster level that caps total allocations below current demand. Not directly evidenced but consistent with the scheduler message.

QUATERNARY — a node or daemonset managing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (e.g., a peer-pods device plugin) is unhealthy or not advertising capacity on the two matching nodes. Consistent with the message but not directly evidenced in this packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient VM quota and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to report all four required evidence fields as missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have no remaining capacity, and the remaining four nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or label selector constraints. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers a peer-pod VM provisioning request that the scheduler cannot fulfill. The pod remains Unschedulable for the full 145-second observation window, so the probe exits without writing any evidence, and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264 (requiredEvidence: orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agent VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs from prior runs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no node can accept a new remote agent pod, and preemption cannot free capacity. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion, not an application code defect. The eval failure and complete absence of evidence are a direct downstream consequence of the pod never starting.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 145s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable/Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, pod stuck for 129s, endedAt 2026-06-19T18:30:36.003Z — the earliest failing check in the sequence, confirming the condition predates the runtime check.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical message to remote-agent-runtime, pod stuck for 145s, endedAt 2026-06-19T18:33:06.174Z — confirms the resource exhaustion persisted across consecutive scheduling attempts.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150219, status=fail — the probe waited the full scheduler timeout before giving up, consistent with a hard scheduling block rather than a transient API error.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent — the eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1918 calls createAgent() which requires a running pod; no pod means no evidence is ever collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — pod scheduling is the first blocking dependency in the remote-agent-runtime probe path.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already at capacity. If the affinity configuration is overly restrictive, expanding eligible nodes could relieve pressure.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs not being cleaned up: if withCleanup() in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs:1916) failed to terminate pods from earlier runs, those pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that should have been released.
Lower probability — a cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm that is set too low for the current eval workload concurrency.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable message if VM capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Also run the sibling checks to confirm all three remote-agent checks reproduce together
reproductionSteps.details: All three checks should fail with the kata.peerpods.io/vm Unschedulable message if the root cause is cluster-wide resource exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations on the 2 eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Identify how many VM slots are allocated vs. capacity. Replace the label selector with the actual affinity key used by remote agent pods.

reproductionSteps.label: List all remote agent pods currently running or pending in the cluster
reproductionSteps.details: Determine whether zombie or leaked pods from prior eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

reproductionSteps.label: Check pending pods and their scheduling events
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector reason=FailedScheduling | grep kata.peerpods.io
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm the scheduling failure is ongoing and not a transient spike.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 0/6 nodes available due to Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 eligible nodes and affinity mismatch on the other 4. All three remote-agent checks are blocked at this layer (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm node resource capacity
affectedAreas.reason: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on both eligible nodes. This is the specific resource named in the Unschedulable message (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at run-status-probes.mjs:1918 calls createAgent() with type 'remote', which produces a pod subject to the node affinity/selector that restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes. The affinity configuration determines which nodes are eligible and therefore how much total VM capacity is available.

affectedAreas.label: Eval probe cleanup path (withCleanup)
affectedAreas.reason: The runner wraps agent creation in withCleanup() at run-status-probes.mjs:1916. If cleanup is not reliably releasing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after each eval run, prior runs may be leaking capacity.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (features.json lines 183-185) are failing with the same scheduling error, indicating the entire remote agent provisioning path is blocked in production-api.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes to determine current VM slot utilization and identify any pods that should have been cleaned up by prior eval runs.

Check whether the withCleanup() path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs is reliably terminating remote agent pods after each eval run; if cleanup is failing silently, leaked pods may be exhausting VM capacity over time.

If VM slots are genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads (not leaked eval pods), escalate to the infrastructure team to either expand kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on existing nodes, add new eligible nodes, or adjust node affinity to allow scheduling on more of the 6 available nodes.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods to determine whether the restriction to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional; if not, relaxing the affinity could increase available scheduling capacity.

Once the scheduling issue is resolved, re-run all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) together to confirm the full provisioning and runtime path recovers end-to-end.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in features.json (line 185), so this check alone does not trigger a feature outage classification; however, remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183-184) and their failure with degradedAfterFailures=1 means the remote-agents feature is currently in a degraded or outage state per the registry contract.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is still active or was transient. A pass would indicate the condition self-resolved; a repeat of the same Unschedulable message confirms ongoing resource exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and allocations on eligible nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly measures available vs. consumed VM slots on all nodes, confirming whether exhaustion is the active constraint.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all remote agent pods currently occupying kata.peerpods.io/vm slots
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep -i remote
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked or zombie pods from prior eval runs are holding capacity that should have been released by withCleanup().

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check FailedScheduling events for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms the scheduling failure is ongoing and shows the frequency and timing of scheduling attempts, helping distinguish a sustained outage from a transient spike.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling dependency
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three checks fail with the same message, it confirms the failure is at the shared scheduling layer rather than in any individual check's probe logic.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling failure would have a different cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request in the pod spec).

If the scheduler message changed to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota exceeded at namespace level, or a different resource name) on a re-run, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would be incorrect.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the cause would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling resource constraint.

If the eval runner logs showed the pod was scheduled successfully but the agent process crashed or returned an unexpected response, the root cause would be in the agent runtime rather than the scheduler.
If no remote agent pods are found running or pending in the cluster, the VM slot exhaustion would need to be explained by a quota or capacity configuration rather than live pod consumption.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a pod-leak detection eval that counts running remote agent pods created by eval runs and alerts if any persist beyond the expected cleanup window, catching withCleanup() failures before they exhaust VM capacity.
Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod selector meets a minimum threshold, catching configuration drift that reduces scheduling headroom.

Consider a synthetic scheduling dry-run eval (kubectl --dry-run=server) that validates a remote agent pod spec can be scheduled without actually consuming VM capacity, providing an early warning before a full provisioning attempt.
